title: Phones, Distractions & Penalties
whatItIs: It's illegal to hold and use a phone, sat nav or any device that can send or receive data while driving, even in a queue. Expect 6 points and a £200 fine.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT use a hand-held phone or similar device for any purpose when driving, even offline.
You MUST NOT pick up and use your phone while stationary in traffic.

keyFacts: You may call 999 or 112 in a genuine emergency if it is unsafe or impractical to stop.
Hands-free is allowed if you never hold the device, but it still distracts you.
Hand-held use: 6 penalty points and a £200 fine. In court, up to £2,500 for a goods vehicle.

keyFacts.text: You MUST keep proper control of your vehicle at all times.

items.title: Hand-held device

items.title: Hands-free

items.title: Sat nav and screens
items.text: Don't be distracted by screens. Stop safely first.

items.title: Other distractions
items.text: Loud music, eating, drinking, smoking, arguing.

items.title: 999 or 112
items.text: Allowed if it's unsafe or impractical to stop.

a.label: Hand-held use
points: Illegal while driving, even when stopped in traffic

b.label: Hands-free use
points: Legal if you don't hold the device at any time
Police can still act if you're distracted and not in control

onTheTest.question: You are queuing in traffic. When may you hold your phone to send a text?
options: When it is in flight mode
onTheTest.why: The ban applies in queues, if the engine cuts out, and offline. You can use it when safely parked.

onTheTest.question: What is the maximum fine a court can give a lorry driver for using a hand-held phone while driving?
onTheTest.why: Highway Code annex 5: maximum £1,000 fine, or £2,500 for a goods vehicle or PCV, plus 6 penalty points.

traps: Stopped in a queue or at lights still counts: the hand-held ban applies.
Flight mode doesn't help: the ban covers devices that are offline.
6 points within 2 years of passing your first driving test: your licence is revoked.
